newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech banking commission seen ending by February.
newsitem.headline: Czech banking commission seen ending by February.

text.p: A 12-member parliamentary commission investigating circumstances around the failure of Czech Kreditni Banka should present its findings by the end of February, the parliamentary press department said on Wednesday.

The commission, established late on Tuesday night by parliament, will comprise four members of the leading governing coalition party, the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), four members of the opposition Social Democrats.

One member from each of the remaining four parties in parliament -- the communists (KSCM), the far-right Republican Party (SPR-RSC), and the two junior coalition members the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) and the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) will also sit on the commission.
A leader of the commission, a topic of heated debate leading up to its formation, has yet to be named.

In August, the Czech National Bank (CNB) rescinded the licence of the insolvent Kreditni Banka with losses estimated at nearly 12 billion crowns after a complicated series of non-performing loans and debt swaps.

Since then, the banking crisis, which also forced the fifth largest bank Agrobanka to be placed under forced central bank administration, has become a political football booted between the central bank, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and the opposition, each blaming the other.
